title: Motion-Aware Reward Modeling for Instruction-Guided Video Editing
abstract: arXiv:2611.22495v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Reward models for instruction-guided video editing can favor temporal consistency at the expense of motion. We study this failure, termed \emph{motion collapse}, using controlled motion-suppression variants of real edits. On VE-Bench, the evaluated composite reward prefers a motion-suppressed candidate in $97\%$ of cases. Learned video rewards and a VLM judge also struggle with mild suppression, while latent optimization and reward-guided fine-tuning exploit this weakness to increase reward as motion declines. A linear probe of our base reward backbone performs near chance on mild suppression, motivating an explicit inter-frame dynamics input. We propose a motion-aware reward model that combines an RGB frame-difference stream with preference training against motion-suppressed and fabricated-motion negatives. translated_title: 面向指令引导视频编辑的运动感知奖励建模
translated_abstract: 指令引导视频编辑的奖励模型可能会偏向时间一致性而牺牲运动效果。我们利用真实编辑的受控运动抑制变体研究了这一被称为“运动坍缩”的失效现象。在VE-Bench上，所评估的复合奖励在97%的情况下更偏好运动被抑制的候选结果。学习型视频奖励模型和VLM评判器在面对轻微运动抑制时同样表现不佳，而潜空间优化和奖励引导的微调则会利用这一弱点，在运动减少的同时提升奖励分数。对我们基础奖励骨干网络的线性探测在轻微抑制上表现接近随机水平，这促使我们引入显式的帧间动态信息输入。我们提出了一种运动感知奖励模型，它将RGB帧差流与针对运动抑制和伪造运动负样本的偏好训练相结合。蒸馏锚点保持了与人类质量判断的一致性。在VE-Bench运动阶梯上，我们的模型降低了（原文在此处截断）……
tldr: 该论文揭示了指令引导视频编辑奖励模型中“运动坍缩”的失效现象——即奖励模型偏向静态一致而牺牲运动，并提出一种结合RGB帧差输入与针对运动抑制负样本进行偏好训练的运动感知奖励模型，从而更好地评估和保持视频编辑中的运动质量。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies the "motion collapse" failure of reward models for instruction-guided video editing, where rewards favor static consistency at the expense of motion, and proposes a motion-aware reward model that combines RGB frame-difference inputs with preference training against motion-suppressed negatives to better evaluate and preserve motion quality in video editing.
